item.title: Body of Dutch man who drown trying to save son in Italy found
item.description:
Body of Dutch man who drown trying to save son in Italy found

July 27, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The body of a Dutch man who dove into Lake Como to save his son was recovered on Sunday, Italian press agency ANSA reports.

The family had taken a rental boat out onto the Italian lake when the man’s 16-year old son dove into the water and had trouble returning to the craft.

The 45-year-old father went into the water to help him but disappeared. The boy was later rescued by someone on a paddle board.

The Italian coast guard spent more than a day searching for the man using sonar and under water cameras. Eventually they recovered his body lying 25 meters deep. The body was taken to a nearby hospital for an investigation.

item.title: Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish
item.description:
Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish

July 24, 2026 Molly Quell

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Johanna van Veen’s gothic horror Blood on Her Tongue offers up a classic vampire tale with some modern contemplations.

The book follows Lucy Goedhart as she is called to the ominously named Zwartwater (black water) estate, where her sister has taken ill. In 1887, there isn’t much in the way of medical treatment, but Lucy’s sister Sarah isn’t fighting off a regular illness.

Sarah has become obsessed with a body found in the bog of the vast estate and since interacting with the 300-year-old corpse she has become increasingly incoherent, struggles with taking care of herself and has developed an insatiable hunger.

As Lucy tries desperately to save her sister, she finds that her sister’s husband, her sister’s doctor and childhood friend, and several other characters who are present at the remote manor house all have their own interests and motivations – some as dangerous as whatever condition is plaguing Sarah.

The book is not for those easily bothered by gore. The title – Blood on Her Tongue – is a pretty good indication of what is to come. Van Veen does not shy away from the horror elements, including two separate scenes of eyeball gouging.

Like any good horror novel, the macabre monster is not the scariest part. The threats Lucy faces are from the men surrounding her sister. Her brother-in-law attempts to seduce Lucy while badgering her to send Sarah away to an asylum.

Sarah’s doctor expresses his own interest in Lucy, pushing his vision of the future while supposedly devoting himself to his patient. The mores of 19th-century upper-class society may be the biggest piece of villainy of all.

In the tradition of Dracula, Blood on Her Tongue tells its story through letters, journal entries and newspaper clippings. The personal correspondence adds to the claustrophobia of the work, with everyone limited to an isolated house, but the media reports remind the reader that the world outside does exist.

The work is the second book from Dutch author Johanna van Veen. It was published in 2025 in English and became a USA Today bestseller. Her first book, My Darling Dreadful Thing, was nominated for the Bram Stoker Award for best horror novel. Van Veen grew up in the Netherlands as a triplet, something that influenced her writing about the sisters Lucy and Sarah.

If horror is your thing, Blood on Her Tongue will creep you out and keep you turning the pages.

You can get your copy at the American Book Center.

item.title: Thousands cross finishing line as Nijmegen Vierdaagse ends
item.description:
Thousands cross finishing line as Nijmegen Vierdaagse ends

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The 108th edition of the Nijmegense Vierdaagse (four-day march) ended on Friday, with tens of thousands of walkers being welcomed with flowers by well-wishers.

British walker Simon Brownlee crossed the finishing line ahead of the rest of the walkers for the 27th time, local media reported. Brownlee, who completed the distance before 10am, told local broadcaster Omroep Gelderland that the walk “felt like home”. “I’m happy it is over and I can now relax,” he said.

Wheelchair participant Ronald van Dort was the very first person to finish, picking up his seventh medal for completing the event.

Over 45,000 walkers from 70 countries took part in this year’s series, which is proving increasingly popular among the young. Ten years ago, 7.5% of the walkers were aged 21 to 30, but this year their number rose to over 20%.

  • Inburgering with DN: the Nijmegen Vierdaagse

This year the event was marred by a fatal shooting just outside the area where the Vierdaagsefeesten, the street festivities accompanying the annual four-day marches, were taking place. One man has been arrested.

The shooting, and other crowd problems, led the organisers to cancel performances by urban scene artists such as Ronnie Flex and Lil’ Kleine because their presence was “attracting the wrong sort of people”, the AD reported.

item.title: Dozens of women forced into prostitution by Romanian gang
item.description:
Dozens of women forced into prostitution by Romanian gang

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dozens of women may have been forced into working as prostitutes in Amsterdam’s red light district by a Romanian gang, Dutch police confirmed on Friday.

The statement follows a joint Dutch and Romanian campaign against human trafficking in the area earlier this month. Seven men were arrested during a string of raids on July 14 – four in the Netherlands and three in Romania. All were Romanian nationals.

Shortly after the arrests, police issued a video interview with one of the victims speaking Romanian, which has led more women to come forward and has resulted in other information reaching the police, the statement said.

Police now say they have spoken to several victims and say they believe more women have been trafficked. They too are said to be Romanian.

The women were lured to Amsterdam with the promise of high earnings but found themselves forced into working in brothels and handing over their earnings to the gang. They were also forced to pay “rent” for their rooms.

None of the men had jobs but were big spenders, buying expensive clothes and cars and gambling heavily, the statement said. The gang also treated part of the red light district as their “personal kingdom”.

Four men remain in custody in the Netherlands, one of whom was extradited from Romania. Another man may also be extradited soon, RTL said. They are all suspected of human trafficking and forming a criminal organisation.

According to the Parool, two of the suspects are half brothers aged 44 and 45 who have earlier convictions for trafficking in women in Romania.

More arrests have not been ruled out.

A year ago, Dutch and Romanian police arrested 13 people in a joint investigation into human trafficking and the forced prostitution of Romanian women, mainly in and around Amsterdam.

item.title: Singer Sophie Straat cleared of discrimination over mosh pit
item.description:
Singer Sophie Straat cleared of discrimination over mosh pit

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Discrimination hotlines in both the Netherlands and Belgium have concluded that Dutch singer Sophie Straat did not discriminate when she asked “all white men to step back” during two of her recent performances.

Last month at the Best Kept Secret festival in Beekse Bergen, Straat — real name Sophie Schwartz — asked for space for women, queer people and people of colour in the “mosh pit”, an area in front of the stage where fans dance chaotically.

She made the same request on Monday during a performance in Ghent, Belgium.

The Dutch discrimination hotline Discriminatie.nl said it received hundreds of complaints but maintains that Straat’s comments do not amount to discrimination against white men based on their colour or gender.

“The call only concerned one short, one-off mosh pit for these groups,” said the hotline. “Therefore, visitors were not refused entry to the concert.”

Belgian authorities reached the same conclusion after receiving some 200 complaints following her performance in Ghent.

“Although the statement may be perceived as polarizing or offensive, in this context it must be seen as a symbolic and artistic expression,” a spokesperson for the Belgian discrimination hotline Unia told the Flemish broadcaster VRT.

“According to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights, artistic and political expressions enjoy broad protection under freedom of expression, even when they provoke, shock or offend.”

Hate messages and death threats

Straat wrote on Instagram earlier this month that she has received “a wave of sexist, antisemitic hate messages and (death) threats, some more explicit and creative than others”.

She has also questioned where the left-wing media has been in all this, saying the public narrative is being controlled by the right.

The singer, who was raised in a Jewish home in Amsterdam’s de Pijp neighbourhood and is known for her protest songs, has said she never wanted to exclude anyone but rather wanted to make room for people who feel unsafe in a mosh pit.

item.title: Youngster arrested for participating in sadistic online network
item.description:
Youngster arrested for participating in sadistic online network

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have arrested a young man from Noord Holland who they suspect of being part of the sadistic online Com network “764”.

The public prosecution department reported the arrest on Thursday, saying the suspect encouraged underage girls to cut themselves and write his online name on a wall with their own blood—so-called “bloodsigns”.

He also is said to have prompted them to write his name on their bodies with a marker, known as“fansigns”. Both are practices within the Com movement—short for The Community—for members to gain prestige.

The suspect himself, who was also charged with aggravated assault, exploitation of underage girls and possession of images of sexual child abuse, was a minor at the time of the alleged crimes. Because of that, no further details are being released.

The Com network consists of various chat groups where members recruit vulnerable young people and force them to commit acts including assault, sexual abuse and murder.

The members, from all corners of the globe, then share images of these acts online in private chat groups, using such platforms as Telegram and Discord.

According to NOS, at least 70 Dutch people are involved in this movement known as “nihilistic extremism” because the incitement to commit such extreme violence doesn’t have a clear ideological motive.

The phenomenon is especially attractive to young men.

item.title: Dangerous drivers face extra surveillance under points system
item.description:
Dangerous drivers face extra surveillance under points system

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The police and justice ministry officials are working on a system which would see traffic offenders being given points for dangerous driving – which will lead to persistent offenders coming under extra surveillance.

Motorists who have collected six points for using a mobile phone while driving or not wearing a seatbelt would come under the tougher regime, RTL Nieuws reported on Friday. No start date has yet been set.

The points will be awarded in addition to regular fines. The number of points will depend on the seriousness of the offences and speeding tickets recorded by camera will not be included.

The new system is being devised in an effort to tackle persistent offenders who do not change their behaviour despite being fined multiple times, RTL said. Last year, almost 30,000 people would have had at least six points if the new system had been in existence.

“Research shows that people who don’t stick to the rules are often responsible for accidents,” Achilles Damen from the public prosecution department told the broadcaster.

The privacy implications of monitoring specific individuals are still being assessed, RTL said.

item.title: Ajax beat Vojvodina in Conference League qualifier, Twente lose
item.description:
Ajax beat Vojvodina in Conference League qualifier, Twente lose

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Ajax kicked off their European football campaign with a 4-1 win over Serbian club Vojvodina in the second qualification round of the Conference League competition in Novi Sad on Thursday evening.

The simple win sets the Amsterdammers up in a strong position ahead of the return match next week. If Ajax win again, they will meet either Irish side Shelbourne FC or Estonian club Nõmme Kalju in the third qualification round for the third-tier European competition.

The Amsterdam goal total included one for 16-year-old debutant Mohamed Abdalla, who became the youngest player to score for a Dutch club in Europe.

There was disappointment for FC Twente, who are hoping to qualify for the group stage of the Europa League. They lost 1-2 at home to Hungarian side Ferencváros and will have to pull out all the stops during the away leg next week to remain in the competition.

If they do lose, Twente will move down to the qualification rounds of the Conference League.

PSV Eindhoven and Feyenoord have qualified directly for the Champions League while NEC is taking part in the qualification competition. AZ, as winners of the KNVB Cup last season, will take part in the Europa League competition.

item.title: Unilever backs London for food division secondary listing
item.description:
Unilever backs London for food division secondary listing

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Unilever’s food division, which is being sold to US sauce and spice producer McCormick, will have a secondary listing on the London stock exchange, despite an intensive lobbying campaign to list in Amsterdam.

Unilever itself has been based in London, and listed there, since 2020.

Unilever said in a statement that the secondary listing is separate to McCormick’s plans to establish an international headquarters in the Netherlands and maintain Unilever Food’s R&D facilities and operations in Wageningen.

This “reflects its commitment to the European market and the critical role the Netherlands will continue to play in the combined company”, the statement said.

Economic affairs minister Heleen Herbert said in a reaction to the sale when it was announced in March that the cabinet had already discussed developments with Unilever and would talk to the new owner “such as about a listing on the Amsterdam stock exchange”.

Unilever’s ice cream arm, spun off in 2024, is listed on the Amsterdam stock exchange as the Magnum Ice Cream Company and is headquartered in the Dutch capital.

The sale of the food arm means there is nothing left of the original Dutch part of Unilever, which was set up in 1930 through the merger of the Dutch Margarine Unie and British soap maker Lever Brothers. Unilever now focuses on personal care and household cleaning products.

item.title: 1.2 million counterfeit cigarettes seized near the German border
item.description:
1.2 million counterfeit cigarettes seized near the German border

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have seized 1.2 million counterfeit cigarettes in a van in the north of the country near the German border.

One person was arrested and the illegal haul was handed over to customs officials for investigation. A cross-border police team discovered the cigarettes during a check on vehicles using the A7 near Bad Nieuweschans.

The mixed patrols feature one German and one Dutch colleague working together in the border region who are authorised to operate in both countries. “This cross-border cooperation allows criminal offences on both sides of the border to be effectively tackled,” Dutch border police said.

So far this year, 106 million illegal cigarettes have been seized by officials, compared with 217 million last year as a whole.

Customs officials announced earlier this month they would crack down on cigarette smuggling. Illegal cigarettes are popular in the Netherlands, where the legal price of tobacco is sky-high.

A packet of 20 cigarettes currently costs over €11 in the Netherlands, and research suggests that an increasing number of smokers are turning to the black market or buying their tobacco products in other countries.
